note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job and Bildad are not portrayed as biblical people but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Bildad answers that Job's words are only wind, that God never twists justice, and that Job's sons got what their own rebellion earned.

sections.meaning: We are only of yesterday and our days are a shadow, so ask the generations before us: they will teach you from the heart.

sections.meaning: He may flourish green in the sun with his roots wrapped round the stones, but once torn up, his place forgets him and others sprout in his place.

sections.meaning: God will not reject the blameless; he will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy, and the tent of the wicked will be gone.

candidates.prompt: In a plain present-day kitchen in daylight, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits slumped at the table with his head in his hands, grieving. Across the table an older friend in a buttoned cardigan leans forward and lectures him sternly, one finger raised, mouth open mid-sentence. Through the window behind them the trees are bending in a strong wind.
An old brass balance scale stands on a plain wooden table in clear, even daylight from a window. Its two pans hang perfectly level and still, exactly balanced. Behind it a plain pale wall.

At dawn, in a wide field that has been burned black, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt kneels and gently presses one small green seedling into the dark soil with both hands. The sky is clearing and soft light falls on the tiny green leaves, the only green thing in the field.

Seen from low down at ground level, a tiny green oak seedling with just two fresh leaves rises from the soil in the middle of the frame, sharp and bright. Directly behind it, softly out of focus, stands the huge trunk and vast spreading crown of a great old oak tree in full summer leaf, filling the sky. Bright midday light.

On the wooden porch of an old farmhouse in warm afternoon light, a very old man with a deeply lined face and white hair sits in a chair speaking earnestly, one hand on his chest and the other open as he explains. Beside him a young man sits leaning forward, listening closely to every word.

At the edge of a wide field in soft afternoon light, a very old white-haired man stands beside a young man, one hand on the young man's shoulder and the other pointing out across the land as he explains something from long experience. The young man listens intently, watching where he points.

A wide marsh that has dried out completely: the ground is cracked pale mud, and in it stands a thick stand of tall papyrus and reeds, still partly green but with their tops already brown and drooping, withering. Hot, hazy daylight. No water anywhere.

A stand of tall papyrus reeds in a marsh. On the left side the reeds stand tall, lush and green in shining water. On the right side the water has dried up to cracked mud, and the reeds there, just as tall, have turned brown and dry and bent over. Clear daylight.

A close view of a large spider's web strung between two dry stalks, glistening with morning dew, but torn wide open in the middle, its broken threads hanging loose where something has fallen straight through it. Soft cool morning light, plain blurred background.

The doorway of an old abandoned wooden house that is sagging and falling in, its roof caved and its walls leaning. Across the open doorway hangs a large spider's web, catching the light. Overcast daylight.

In bright morning sun, a lush, vigorous green vine full of fresh leaves and new shoots spreads across a garden and climbs over a low wall. At its base its thick roots wind round and grip a heap of grey stones. Everything about it looks strong and thriving.

A young tree full of bright green leaves grows straight out of an old dry-stone wall in strong sunlight, its roots twisted round and between the grey stones, its branches spreading wide over the garden beyond.

A large leafy vine has been torn out of the ground by its roots and lies wilting across a heap of grey stones, beside the raw, empty hole where it grew. In the fresh soil all round the hole, many small new green seedlings are already sprouting. Plain overcast daylight.

A garden bed in soft daylight: in the middle is a bare patch of freshly turned earth and loose stones where a big plant once grew, with only a few torn roots left in it. All round the bare patch, other young plants are already growing in and filling the space.

In a sunlit green meadow under a bright clear sky, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt throws his head back and laughs out loud with pure joy, his eyes creased and his mouth wide open, his whole face lit.
On a green hilltop in bright clear morning light, a grey-haired man in a plain shirt raises both arms high and shouts for joy, his face full of laughter, green fields spreading out below him.
